scenes.title: The plan

scenes.title: Key ideas
items: Audits review specific code at a specific time
Bug bounties pay hackers to report instead of exploit
scenes.vo: First, Common failure types: logic bugs, reentrancy (a contract is called back before it updates its state), broken access control, and economic exploits (correct code, exploitable incentives or oracles). Next, Audits review specific code at a specific time. Check the scope (which contracts), date (before later changes?), severity of findings and whether they were fixed. Then, Bug bounties pay hackers to report instead of exploit. A large, active bounty is a good sign. And finally, Time and value at risk: code that has safely held large value for years has survived more real attacks.

scenes.title: Worked example
steps: The newest code is unaudited and the bounty is small relative to the value.
scenes.vo: Let's work an example, step by step. Protocol X: two audits, but the latest upgrade (last month) isn't in either scope; bounty $50k; T.V.L. $400M. The newest code is unaudited and the bounty is small relative to the value. Size down, or wait.

scenes.title: Checklist
items: Audit scope matches deployed code; date after last upgrade
Bug bounty size relative to TVL checked
scenes.vo: Here's your checklist. Do it now, for real. First, Audit scope matches deployed code; date after last upgrade. Next, Critical/high findings resolved. And finally, Bug bounty size relative to T.V.L. checked.

scenes.q: What does an audit not prove?
scenes.a: That the code (or later changes, or economic design) is safe.
